short: Sweden's last major battlefield victory in the Great Northern War.
full:
Fought on 20 December 1712, the Battle of Gadebusch pitted a Swedish army under Magnus Stenbock against a combined Danish and Saxon force. Stenbock had crossed into Germany with a newly raised army in an attempt to relieve the besieged Swedish garrisons in Pomerania. Near Gadebusch, he encountered the allied army and launched a determined attack.

Supported by effective artillery fire, the Swedish infantry broke the Danish and Saxon lines, securing a resounding victory. However, the triumph was short-lived; Stenbock's army was unable to break the broader strategic encirclement and was eventually forced to surrender at Tönning the following year, crippling Sweden's ability to project power in Germany.
